name: Smith Machine Reverse-Grip Bench Press
description: The Smith Machine Reverse-Grip Bench Press performs the supinated grip bench press on a Smith machine, which provides a stable bar path for this mechanically weaker grip position. The fixed path makes this upper-chest and triceps emphasis variation considerably safer to attempt alone compared to its free-barbell counterpart.

execution.starting_position: Lie on a flat bench under the Smith machine bar. Take a supinated (underhand) grip with palms facing toward the head. Grip inside shoulder-width for comfort.
execution.setup_instructions: Set the Smith machine bar at the appropriate height. The fixed bar path makes this variation much more manageable than its free-bar version. Reduce load significantly from your standard bench max.
steps: Step 1: Rotate the bar off the hooks with a supinated grip.
Step 2: Lower under control to the lower chest with elbows tracking close to the body.
Step 4: Rotate and rerack after the final rep.
execution.breathing_instructions: Inhale and brace before descent. Exhale at lockout.
common_mistakes: Gripping too wide — the supinated grip places wrists under severe stress if too wide
Trying to use the same load as a standard bench press
safety_considerations: The supinated grip is weaker — reduce load by 20% or more
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Full touch to lower chest; full elbow extension.
coaching_cues: Elbows track toward your sides, not outward
Feel the upper chest and triceps working, not just the shoulders
